en-GB.name: Snapjaw
en-GB.subtitle: Feed the flytrap. Spare bees.
en-GB.description:
Your iPhone Duo is a Venus flytrap.

Open your phone and the trap opens: the two halves are its lobes and the hinge is its midrib. Bugs fly in and land on the glistening nectar to sip. Close your phone and the trap closes with it: CHOMP. Every bug still inside is caught. But bees love nectar too, and you must never eat a bee.

The trick is choosing your moment, then meaning it. Wait for a crowd and close without dithering: the flies feel the lobes coming, and a slow, hesitant close lets them escape. A half close never bites, so it is all or nothing. While the phone is shut, the outer screen shows your catch. Open it again to keep feeding.

No Duo? Every other iPhone plays the whole game: tap to snap.

No ads. No in-app purchases. No accounts. No data collected. Pay once and it's yours.

30 LEVELS
Hand-made levels in three worlds: Morning Bog, Dusk and Night. The first five teach one idea each; then come ant marches, gnat clouds, moths, wasps, dragonflies and the bugs of the night. Every level has one clear goal and up to three stars, and stars open the next world. The Night is hard.

ENDLESS
The arcade run, from morning to night, until your snaps run out. The bugs change with the light: houseflies and gnats at breakfast, ladybirds and grasshoppers by noon, moths and dragonflies at dusk, fireflies and crickets in the dark, and now and then a rare Golden Scarab.
• Snaps are what you spend. A run starts with 12 (a few more in your first runs), you hold up to 14, and every bite costs one
• Catch 3 or more bugs in one bite for a Feast and win a snap back. Catch 5 or more in a clean bite for a FEAST: double score and two snaps back
• Score = the bugs' points × the number of bugs × your chain
• Every clean bite of 2 or more bugs grows the chain, all the way to ×5. An empty bite, a bug that gets away or a bee in the bite starts it again
• A bee in the bite is let go, unharmed and cross, and costs an extra snap. A wasp stings: two extra
• Keep a bug waiting too long and a snap wilts
• When the snaps run out, your trap is tired. One more go?

GOALS AND GROWTH
Three goals are always on the go, from a pool of 39: a 5-bug bite, spare 8 bees in one run, catch a firefly at night, and more. Each one you complete grows your plant through 12 ranks, from Sprout to Bog Monarch; all three in one run earns a bonus.

THE GARDEN
Grow 8 flytraps: Classic, Red Dragon, B52, Sawtooth, Shark Tooth, Fused Tooth, Cupped Trap and, for a Bog Monarch only, Golden Glow. Some grow as you rank up; others are won with a special goal. Pick one and it's your trap everywhere. Same bite, new look.

THE BUG BOOK
16 species, each with a drawing and a one-line joke. Catch a bug to add its page; bees and wasps go in when you spare them.

DAILY BOG
The same bugs for everyone, every day, and one try that counts. Play day after day to grow your streak, and share your score with friends. Then practise as much as you like.

ZEN BOG
No rush, no end. Snaps never run out, nothing wilts, and a bee costs you nothing but your chain. Catch at your own pace and stop whenever you like. No leaderboard.

MADE FOR THE FOLD. PLAYS ON OTHER iPhone MODELS TOO.
On iPhone Duo, hold it any way you like, landscape or portrait, open wide or part way. Every round starts with the phone closed: open it and the bugs arrive. The bite lands as the halves meet, so a gentle close catches as much as a hard one. On any other iPhone, tap anywhere to snap.

SOUND AND FEEL
The CHOMP, every buzz and hum, the frogs by day and the crickets at night are all synthesised live in the app. You feel the bite in your hands the moment the halves meet. Sound, haptics, the silent switch and Reduce motion each have a setting.

GAME CENTER
Leaderboards for your Best Score and the Daily Bog, and 12 achievements. Optional: Snapjaw works fully without signing in.

review.notes:
Thanks for reviewing Snapjaw: a paid game with no ads, no in-app purchases, no accounts, no data collection and no network requests of its own. Nothing needs a login or a demo account.

1. TESTING WITHOUT AN iPHONE DUO (start here)
You don't need a Duo. The whole game works on any iPhone and in the Simulator, by touch.
- Control: tap anywhere to snap the trap. It opens again by itself.
- Home: Play starts the next level (Level 1 first). Also Endless, Daily, Zen, Levels (the map), Bug Book, Garden, Settings.
- Quickest look (3 minutes): Play (Level 1: one fly, tap while it sips), Level 2, then Home > Endless.
- Bugs land on the gold nectar drops. A tap catches every bug inside the trap. Score = points x bugs x chain (up to x5), so waiting for a crowd pays.
- Bees, bumblebees and wasps wear a white halo. Never eat them: a bee in a bite is let go unharmed and costs an extra snap.
- Endless: 12 snaps to start (up to 14 in a new player's first runs), 14 at most, 1 per bite; 3+ bugs in one bite (a Feast) earn snaps back. At 0, "Your trap is tired" and the results show.
- Levels: 30 in 3 worlds (Morning Bog, Dusk, Night), each with one goal, a bite limit and 1 to 3 stars. They open in order; 20 stars open Dusk, 40 the Night. Levels 1 to 5 teach one idea each; no forced tutorial. Later levels are meant to be hard.

2. HOW THE HINGE IS USED (iPhone Duo)
Snapjaw reads the hinge angle and status only through the public iOS 27.1 API (SwiftUI onHingeChange), behind an availability check. No private API. They are used only while playing and are never stored or sent anywhere.
a) The phone is the trap: open phone, open trap. Every round starts closed: if the Duo is open, the screen says "Close the phone to start"; open it again and the bugs come.
b) To bite, close the phone. The bite fires once, as the halves meet (about 18 degrees, or when iOS reports it closed). A partial close never bites. Opening re-arms the trap.
c) While shut, the run is frozen and the outer display shows a CHOMP card with the catch and "Open to keep feeding".
d) Any pose plays (landscape, portrait, any angle). No pose card, no penalty.
e) The score sits on the right half; Settings > Score on the left moves it.

3. KIND TO THE DEVICE (Guidelines 2.4.2 and 1.4.5)
- A bite is closing the phone, the ordinary way a foldable is closed every day. Force is never measured: the bite fires as the halves meet, so a gentle close catches as much as a hard one. Nothing asks the player to slam, shake or press the phone.
- Bites are limited (12 snaps to start, 14 at most; each level has a bite limit), so the game rewards waiting, not closing often. The Zen Bog has no limit and no timer.
- Flies flee a slow, hesitant close, but no score, achievement or leaderboard rewards closing speed or the number of closes.

4. MODES AND PROGRESS (nothing hidden, nothing to buy)
- Endless: waves from morning to night, until the snaps run out.
- Daily Bog: the same bugs for everyone; one scored try a day, then practice; a streak; Share opens the iOS share sheet with one line of text.
- Zen Bog: relaxed and endless; snaps never run out, nothing wilts, no leaderboard. Pause > End shows the results.
- Goals: three at a time on Home (shown once you have played a little), from 39. Garden: 8 cosmetic flytraps. Bug Book: 16 species. 12 cosmetic plant ranks.

5. CONTENT
A cartoon flytrap catching cartoon bugs, the way a frog catches flies. No blood or injury; bees and wasps are always let go unharmed.

6. PRIVACY
No SDKs, analytics, ads or tracking. Progress stays on the device; Share sends nothing itself. App Privacy: Data Not Collected.

7. GAME CENTER
Optional. 2 leaderboards (Best Score from Endless, and the Daily Bog; Zen and Levels submit none), 12 achievements (575 points), none hidden.

8. OTHER
- No notifications. Debug and demo modes are disabled in Release builds.
- Sound plays with the silent switch on; Settings > Respect silent switch turns that off.

nomination.name: Snapjaw - App Launch - iPhone Duo Venus flytrap game
nomination.description:
Snapjaw turns iPhone Duo into a Venus flytrap. The phone is the trap: open it and the lobes open, the hinge is the midrib, and bugs land on the glistening nectar to sip. Close the phone and the trap closes with it: CHOMP. While it is shut, the outer display shows the catch; open it again to keep feeding.

It's a game of choosing, not hitting. Wait for a crowd and catch them all in one bite, close decisively or the flies escape, and never eat a bee. 30 hand-made levels across Morning Bog, Dusk and Night teach it, then test it, with up to three stars each. Endless runs pass from morning to night with new bugs, and a Bug Book of 16 species waits to be filled.

Three goals at a time grow your plant through 12 ranks and a Garden of 8 flytraps. A Daily Bog with a streak, a Zen Bog that never ends, and Game Center. Other iPhones play by tapping. Every sound is synthesized in the app. No ads, no in-app purchases, no data collected.
nomination.notes: Optimized for iPhone Duo. Public iOS 27.1 hinge API, read literally: open phone, open trap. The bite fires as the halves meet; a partial close never bites and force is never measured, so a gentle close works. Every round starts closed, any pose plays (landscape or portrait) and the outer display shows a CHOMP card while shut. Bites are limited, so patience beats closing often. Levels 1 to 5 teach by doing. Also from us: Squish, Brim, Swoop and Hush.
